newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Vendex bids 2.5 billion francs for BIS.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Vendex bids 2.5 billion francs for BIS.

text.p: Dutch retail and business services group Vendex International said on Monday it planned to buy French temporary employment agency BIS, valuing the company at 2.5 billion francs ($472.6 million).

Vendex said it had agreed with the family of BIS founder Laurent Negro to acquire their 60 percent stake in the company for 490 francs per share. It will soon make a public bid at the same price for the remaining shares listed on the Paris bourse.
The bid will be paid in cash from existing credit lines and would have a moderately positive effect on Vendex's earnings per share in the 1997/1998 financial year, it added.
Earlier, shares in both companies were suspended amid market speculation of a bid.
Vendex shares rose sharply when trading was resumed at 1100 GMT, climbing 7.70 guilders to 84.50 shortly after trading resumed. ($ = 5.290 French Francs)
